The aim is high accuracy with as few parameters as possible. On MNIST the method reached 99.44 percent accuracy with 6.2k parameters. On CIFAR10 it reached 92.2 percent with 157.8k parameters.
arxiv-2603-20359: Calvello and co-authors build theory for data-driven smoothing and forecasting of dynamical systems. Machine learning methods for data assimilation show promise, but their analysis lags behind. Their framework first proves the target mapping exists. It then studies how neural operator designs approximate that mapping. Together, these steps yield new universal approximation theorems. Tests use the Lorenz 63, Lorenz 96, and Kuramoto-Sivashinsky systems. The results give data-driven methods a firmer footing for forecasting work.
arxiv-2603-20959: Renganathan and Booth estimate small failure probabilities with fewer costly tests. Standard methods first train a surrogate model, then build a sampling plan with fresh tests. Their single stage method trains a Gaussian process surrogate and a sampling density from the same shared tests. The KDE-AIS method adapts the sampling density with kernel density estimation. They prove it converges to the optimal zero variance density. In experiments, it beats leading methods on accuracy per test spent.
arxiv-2603-21259: Batte and Kaggwa determine which Lucas numbers can be built by mixing Fibonacci and Lucas numbers in base b concatenation. They study two Diophantine equations that join a Fibonacci number and a Lucas number digit by digit. Tools from Diophantine approximation, using linear forms in logarithms, combine with reduction methods from continued fractions. The argument shows only finitely many such Lucas numbers exist. The work pins down the full set of solutions for both mixed concatenation forms.
arxiv-2603-21559: Kang and co-authors improve weakly-supervised video scene graph generation, which parses videos into relational triplets without box annotations. Off-the-shelf detectors propose every visible object, flooding relation models with pairs that never interact. Their fix learns a pair affinity score: how likely two objects are to interact. That score guides ranking at inference and modulates the context reasoning itself. A matching scheme uses vision-language grounding to clean up pseudo-labels. On the Action Genome benchmark, the additions lifted several baselines to state-of-the-art results.
arxiv-2603-21759: McCarthy studies whether the classical permutation group sits maximally inside the quantum permutation group. Banica and Bichon conjectured that it does, but proof exists only for small cases. By duality, any counterexample needs an exotic partition category between the non-crossing and all-partition categories. Such a category must contain combinations of crossing-partition vectors. McCarthy proves generation results for categories built from those vectors. No exotic category can use a combination of just three crossing vectors. At N equals 6, a 31-vector combination also fails to yield one.
arxiv-2603-22159: Rice and Yeates improve a solar wind outflow model of the Sun's coronal magnetic field. The standard PFSS model ignores the wind. Their Outflow Fields model gave better open flux values and streamer shapes in earlier work. Here they tune the model with an evolutionary algorithm. They check it against eclipse photos and a wider set of observations. From 2000 to 2022, it cuts the flux mismatch from about 45% to 24%. The model ships as a Python package named outflowpy.
arxiv-2603-22359: Shen and Shen present STEM Agent, a modular frame for building AI agent systems. Most frameworks lock in one protocol, one tool plan, and a fixed user model early. STEM instead grows from a plain core, like a stem cell taking a role. Specialized handlers, tool bindings, and memory parts compose into a full system. One gateway unifies five interop protocols. A Caller Profiler keeps learning user tastes across more than twenty dimensions. A 413-test suite checks the whole build in under three seconds.
arxiv-2603-22559: Bittner shows that the classic area laws of thermodynamics come from one geometric object. In the pressure-volume plane, work over a cycle equals the enclosed area. Heat has a twin law in the temperature-entropy plane. He proves both laws are projections of a single two-form on the space of equilibrium states. The same frame ties cycle work to local curvature of the energy surface, readable from measured response values. It also reaches toward fluctuation results from stochastic thermodynamics.
arxiv-2603-22959: Griesbauer and co-authors propose stepwise variational inference with vine copulas. Variational inference approximates a posterior, often with weak dependence structure. Vine copulas build dependence from nested trees of simple copulas. The authors estimate the approximation tree by tree, step by step. The usual divergence fails to recover the right parameters here. They define the training bound with Rényi divergence instead. A stopping rule decides when to add more trees. The method sits between mean-field and full dependence, using few parameters.
arxiv-2603-23159: Nguyen and co-authors present conformal cross-modal active learning for vision models. Active learning cuts labeling cost by picking the most useful samples. Most methods ignore the language knowledge inside vision-language models. Their method uses a pretrained vision-language teacher for the uncertainty scores. Conformal calibration makes those scores trustworthy for sample choice. A vision-only student learns from the picked labels. Diversity-aware selection adds a second filter. Tests across benchmarks beat top active learning baselines on data efficiency.
arxiv-2603-23259: Border and three co-authors model how heart and breathing rhythms sync in the body. The brain steers both rhythms while they interact through the lung blood vessels. That sync shows up as respiratory sinus arrhythmia. The team models the electrical and elastic links to find when sync sets in. They find that sync cuts cardiac power losses by 10% in humans. In other species the saving reaches 55%. They compare the predicted output gain with gains seen when pacing restores the rhythm.
arxiv-2603-23359: Ghosh and seventeen co-authors report late-time polarimetry of the gamma-ray burst afterglow GRB 250129A. They used the Southern African Large Telescope about 19 hours after the burst. The data hint at linear polarization, with no swing in its angle across wavelengths. Early polarization is common when a reverse shock rules, but models show that shock fades within 100 seconds. The late glow instead fits an off-axis view of a jet with a Gaussian core and wings. The burst thus links late polarization to jet shape.
arxiv-2603-23559: Chen and six co-authors build ReCAP, a screen agent that can solve CAPTCHAs. Native GUI agents read screenshots and act directly, yet CAPTCHAs trip them up. Special solver pipelines exist, but they cannot do general screen work. ReCAP trains on machine-made interaction trails paired with reasoning text. A testbed of seven CAPTCHA types stresses the skills. Failed trails become self-correction lessons, teaching recovery from mid-task slips. ReCAP lifts CAPTCHA success a lot over its base agents. General screen skill stays strong in the tests.
arxiv-2603-23959: Pillai settles an open case about when Matérn random fields can be told apart on bounded domains. For fields in four dimensions, two models can share the same microergodic parameter yet use different scales. Zhang and Anderes had settled dimensions below three and above four, but four stayed open. Pillai proves the two Gaussian measures are mutually singular on any bounded domain. His proof uses localized Fourier coefficients and a normalized Whittle score. The method may help with identifiability in other spatial models.
arxiv-2603-24259: Sire and Pereira add uncertainty estimates to spline prediction on curved surfaces. Spline interpolation fits smooth phenomena by minimizing an energy tied to the Laplacian. Their method builds the spline on a compact Riemannian manifold. A link to universal kriging lets them treat the fit as a Gaussian random field, so simulations reflect prediction doubt. The field needs the spectrum of the Laplace-Beltrami operator, which is usually unknown. A finite element triangulation supplies it, and local metric changes add anisotropy. Tests use temperature on a sphere and a cylinder.
arxiv-2603-24359: Janzen and co-authors study how gender cues in prompts affect language-model code generation and review. They run three studies: real-world coding prompts, a controlled user study, and a simulated review setup. Female-authored prompts use more indirect and involved language, they find. That style does not lead to consistent gaps in correctness or static code quality. Review is another story. Models approve female-authored code more on average, at equal quality. Prompt style also shifts code length and maintainability in controlled tests.
arxiv-2603-24459: de Jongh and co-authors study how to shrink avalanches in the two-dimensional Abelian sandpile model. The model is a classic case of self-organised criticality, where small triggers cause large cascades like stylised earthquakes. An external controller may remove sand grains at chosen sites to calm the system. The team gives a rigorous method to compute the expected avalanche size from a connected patch of critical sites. For square patches, they characterise the best intervention sites, which balance cutting the largest avalanches against calming more of them.
arxiv-2603-24659: Sbarrato and co-authors present BLAZ4R, the first living catalog of blazars beyond redshift four. Such blazars probe how supermassive black holes and relativistic jets evolved in the first two billion years. X-ray data from eROSITA anchor the catalog, since X-rays best constrain jet power at these distances. The catalog holds 54 blazars with X-ray properties, radio spectra, and multiwavelength profiles. Jetted sources prove far more common, relative to non-jetted ones, than at low redshift, the authors report.
arxiv-2603-25159: Kim, Lee, and Cho build one model that spots defects in 3D scans across many object types. Training uses only normal point clouds. A single shared model tends to blur types together, so rebuilt shapes borrow the wrong traits and scores turn shaky. Their design fights that blur in three ways. Tokens give each item a semantic name tag. Contrast training pulls type meanings apart. A geometry-guided decoder then rebuilds each scan true to its type. On two benchmarks it tops both shared and per-type models.
arxiv-2603-25259: Tebaldi and co-authors steer a mobile robot arm so it stores as little kinetic energy as possible while working near people. A wheeled base plus an arm has extra freedom, which makes control design tricky. Their method plans whole-body motion around a least-energy goal, aimed at physical human-robot tasks. They test it on a peg-in-hole job. The robot ends with less stored energy than under a benchmark method. System performance improves at the same time.
arxiv-2603-25759: Řada, Velichová, and Zamboj visualize Minkowski point set operations in four dimensions. Here the Minkowski product is taken as the quaternionic product. They draw selected point sets with two projection tools. One is double orthogonal projection, and the other is perspective projection, both from 4D to 3D. The sets they generate include circles, which form a Clifford torus and a 3-sphere. Other sets give lines that form a quadratic cone. Some sets contain both circles and lines.
arxiv-2603-26259: Edy, Conti, and Macé study two quirks of late interaction search models. First, they test a length bias that can arise when multi-vector scores are pooled. Second, they look at the spread of similarity scores past the best match used by the MaxSim rule. Tests on NanoBEIR show the bias holds for causal models, and can hit two-way models in extreme cases. They also find no strong trend past the top token, which supports the MaxSim rule.
arxiv-2603-26359: Finger and co-authors use an AI platform to discover quantum algorithms for molecular ground states. The Hive platform drives language models through a broad evolutionary search for new programs. The search finds heuristic quantum circuits for lithium hydride, water, and fluorine molecules. These circuits use far fewer quantum resources than leading near-term methods. The team studies which parts drive the gains, then runs the circuits on a Quantinuum H2 machine to gauge what hardware chemical accuracy needs.
arxiv-2603-26559: Yokoi and co-authors test helicity-based subgrid models for large-eddy simulation of turbulence. The classic Smagorinsky model often drains too much energy, even with dynamic tuning. Helicity, the link between velocity and vorticity, adds shape data that plain energy measures miss. The team checks helicity models against direct numerical simulations, with and without net rotation. Forcing holds large-scale helicity gradients in place during the runs. They find helicity effects should join the eddy viscosity term to model small-scale turbulence well.
arxiv-2603-26659: Das, Byrd, Baek, and Ha teach a legged robot to push a cart by copying only part of a walking style. Stable walking and precise pushing pull against each other during learning. First they train a rugged walking policy with wide domain and terrain randomisation. The pushing policy then imitates just the lower-body motion through a partial adversarial prior. In IsaacLab tests the robot pushes a cart along varied paths, and the skill transfers to MuJoCo. The method proves steadier and more exact than the baselines tried.
arxiv-2603-27659: Collins and Yuan bound norms for multi-leg matrix tensors. They study extreme values of traced tensor products. A diagram method frames both upper and lower bounds. Bounds scale as powers of the factor dimension. Permutation matrices hit the lower bounds exactly. Proofs start with two factors and extend to any count. Open indices yield matrix bounds for all moments. One coefficient choice attains every lower bound. Random matrix uses follow from the bounds.
arxiv-2603-27859: Akylzhanov tackles the tokenizer tax on Kazakh text in language models. Kazakh splits into far more tokens than English does. That waste shrinks context and blurs word structure. KazByte feeds raw bytes through a small adapter instead. The adapter learns to speak to a frozen Qwen2.5-7B. Attention layers then fine-tune on Kazakh text. The hypothesis claims parity or better on benchmarks. Validation is still ongoing in this design report.
arxiv-2603-28059: Cheban studies remotely almost periodic motion, a weakening of the classic almost periodic idea for dynamical systems. He proves basic properties of such motions and extends Amerio's well-known theorem to this abstract setting. The theorem links remote almost periodicity of a system's motions to that of its limit motions. Cheban then applies the general results to several classes of nonlinear differential, difference, and algebraic equations.
arxiv-2603-28259: Suresh and Suresh release PyEncode, an open-source library that loads structured data into quantum states with small circuits. General encoders need a gate count that explodes with vector size. Many real vectors, though, follow one of ten exact patterns, from sparse to Fourier to polynomial. PyEncode maps each pattern to a checked Qiskit circuit, with no rounding and no full vector built. It also predicts gate counts and offers ways to combine patterns.
arxiv-2603-28459: Dongre and Gunderman study error-correcting codes for quantum devices whose sites hold different numbers of levels. Most code theory assumes every site is the same. Mixed registers break that mold, and some patterns turn out to be impossible. The authors prove general facts about mixed Pauli operators and list forbidden encoded forms. They then build optimal mixed-register stabilizer codes by joining codes on coprime local dimensions. The resulting logical spaces match none of the parts.
arxiv-2603-29059: Pial and co-authors report on building embeddings of a full nation scale social network. They work with the population network of the Netherlands. Such networks are large, multiplex, and time dependent, which poses hard technical issues. A layer sensitive random walk strategy improves on flattening methods for such data. An alignment step brings annual networks into one embedding space without leaking future data. Fibonacci spirals and whitening give more balanced splits. The methods proved useful on models for 13 downstream tasks.
arxiv-2603-29259: Huang and co-authors study how to align a recommender with user likes and dislikes. The setting is sequential and multimodal, so items come as text and images over time. In implicit feedback, an unseen item is not a sure dislike. That makes preference training hard to set up well. The team tests ways to pick negative items. Sampling from a shifting top-K pool beat fixed hard negatives. This cut false dislike signals but kept hard cases. Their method, RoDPO, gained up to 5.25 percent in NDCG@5 scores.
arxiv-2603-29359: Yun and co-authors tackle crowded satellite downlinks in low Earth orbit. Users sit in a narrow angular range, so channels correlate strongly. That crowding makes the channel matrix ill-conditioned. Their analysis ties the smallest eigenvalue to user density. A sharp threshold emerges where zero-forcing precoding fails. Their fix, space-time adaptive beamforming, uses Doppler shifts as a new signal dimension. A user selection method exploits both space and Doppler gaps. Simulations show large sum-rate gains in dense settings.
arxiv-2603-29559: Ferrer and co-authors ask when a language model grader can be trusted. Rather than raise grading accuracy, they predict when the grader is likely right. High-confidence grades can then auto-process, and shaky ones go to humans. They compare three confidence routes: self-reported scores, self-consistency votes, and token probabilities. Seven models grade three education datasets. Self-reported confidence calibrated best in every condition. Voting cost five times more yet calibrated worse. Bigger models calibrated better, though gains varied by dataset.
arxiv-2603-29659: Yuan and Li present a self-scaling tensor basis neural network for Reynolds stress in wall-bounded turbulence. Tensor basis networks are a grounded way to close RANS simulations. Their weak point is robustness across Reynolds numbers and shapes. The new model normalizes inputs with velocity-gradient invariants. That gives a built-in scale with no empirical coefficients or wall distance. The form keeps Galilean and rotational invariance. Tests on channel and hill flows matched simulation data closely. A model trained at low Reynolds number generalized to higher ones.
arxiv-2603-29859: Stolfi, Onofri, and Bretti use Bayesian tools to fit water uptake models for porous materials. Sparse absorption data must reveal hydraulic parameters in a hard inverse problem. The forward model is a degenerate parabolic equation with boundary-driven flow. The fit landscape is non-convex, with some parameters barely identifiable. They use approximate Bayesian computation with sequential Monte Carlo instead. Posterior shapes then expose which parameter mixes the data constrain. Tests on synthetic and real lab samples confirm sound recovery.
arxiv-2604-00559: Chi introduces FecalFed, a federated-learning framework for poultry disease detection that guards farm data privacy. Early detection of highly pathogenic avian influenza and endemic poultry diseases matters for global food security. Computer vision can classify disease from fecal images, but farm privacy worries and data silos block large-scale use. Public farm datasets also often hide severe, undocumented contamination. Chi curates and releases a deduplicated set of 8,770 images across four disease classes. The set exposes a 46.89 percent duplication rate in popular public repositories.
arxiv-2604-00859: Tang and colleagues run a sensitivity study of K1(1270) decay modes using semileptonic D-meson decays, taking the BESIII experiment as a case study. They analyze four three-body final states at once and propose a model-independent determination of the branching fraction for K1(1270) decaying to anti-K pi pi. The approach needs no detailed knowledge of intermediate resonant contributions.
arxiv-2604-00959: Miramontes, Morgado, and Papavassiliou compute space-like baryonic form factors of the pion and kaon using the Bethe-Salpeter formalism. In the exact isospin-symmetric case this quantity is forbidden by G-parity. Any nonzero signal therefore directly probes the quark mass difference between down and up quarks. Their pion baryonic radius comes out at 0.043 fm, consistent with dispersive benchmarks, while kaon radii show a larger spatial extent, compatible with chiral QCD models.
arxiv-2604-01359: Mantsivoda and Gavrilina propose world-centered multi-agent systems in place of agent-centered designs. Firms and public bodies need a shared, clear picture of the world that stays stable over time. In their scheme, learning and teamwork run over one common world model rather than lone agent-local views, giving global consistency and behavior open to checks. They sort worlds by features such as how clear their ontology is and how normative they are, describe them with semantic models, and present the Ontobox platform as a version.
arxiv-2604-01459: Shah and Cortes enable Koopman subspace pruning in a Reproducing Kernel Hilbert Space via principal angles and vectors. Data-driven models of the Koopman map rely on projections, where scores hinge on subspace invariance. Subspace pruning discards skewed directions to improve invariance, measured by the largest principal angle between the subspace and its image. Current techniques are largely restricted to Euclidean settings. They outline an exact routine, scaled for sets with random Nystrom methods. They introduce the Kernel-SPV and Approximate Kernel-SPV algorithms for subspace refinement via those vectors.
arxiv-2604-01659: Ma and colleagues present AURA, a multimodal shared autonomy method for urban navigation that splits the job into human-led direction and AI-led control. Existing shared autonomy approaches usually put humans and AI in one action space, which raises cognitive load. AURA's Spatial-Aware Instruction Encoder lines up varied human instructions with what the system sees and where things are. Tests in simulation and the real world show AURA follows human instructions, reduces manual effort, and improves navigation stability. Shared autonomy reduces takeovers by more than 44 percent.
arxiv-2604-01959: Medvedev and Proskurnikov design an impulsive controller keeping a simple continuous plant's output inside a set corridor. The plant, a scalar linear model, is the simplest picture of chemical kinetics, used in control and drug dosing, and extends to Wiener forms. Because the controller fires only at spaced instants, varying dose size and spacing, the closed loop mixes continuous and discrete dynamics with nonlinear effects. Their method builds a stable periodic 1-cycle whose orbit matches the corridor, with local and global attraction proved, and paracetamol dosing shows the approach.
arxiv-2604-02059: Crokidakis models collective attention under digital exposure. A variable tracks sustained focus, with recovery competing with screen harm. The digital setting acts as an external control. A linear version gives a baseline, and a curved term captures growth under intense use. Steady focus falls as screen use rises, and a potential shows overstimulation warping the landscape with no second stable state. It needs no spread between people or twin states, but describes a slow shift under pressure.
arxiv-2604-02659: Pourkamali-Anaraki improves low-rank compression of pretrained models. Exact singular value decomposition costs too much for large weight matrices. Randomized SVD falters when singular values decay slowly, a common case in modern models. His randomized subspace iteration adds power steps to sharpen spectral separation and control error. He also ties compression error to prediction error through softmax perturbations, and tests the method on convolutional networks. The goal is smaller models that still answer well.
arxiv-2604-03059: Acerbi and colleagues present the acquisition system for DarkSide-20k, a liquid-argon dark matter search at Gran Sasso. The detector combines a dual-phase time projection chamber, vetoes and 2720 photomultiplier channels. The system digitises waveforms continuously without triggers, with high single-photoelectron efficiency and processing to cut data. CAEN VX2745 digitisers with firmware run the readout, timed across 48 units by a rubidium standard. A Quadrant, one quarter of the system, validated at TRIUMF, sustains readout beyond physics rates.
arxiv-2604-03259: Chen and colleagues survey AI-driven psychology work, a field whose yearly papers grew from 859 in 2000 to 29,979 by 2025. They sort tasks by how they compute, not by topic, into classification, regression, structured relational, and generative interactive types. Drawing on over 300 works across the pretrained and language-model eras, they surface shared methods and open problems in reading models, privacy, and validity across cultures.
arxiv-2604-03459: Debeire and colleagues present PC-AFM, a physics-constrained generative downscaler for local climate detail at km scales. Soft balance rules keep precipitation and moisture in line with large-scale inputs, while a gradient trick stops the rules from fighting the generative goal. Outside its training range, the model halves rain wet bias and improves extreme scores without any target-climate data at run time.
arxiv-2604-04059: Islem Khemissi and team mined agent-authored pull request references from the AIDev dataset to map how humans and agents cite each other's work. Humans start most references to agent-authored pull requests, yet a large share of the exchanges are AI-assisted, forming meta-collaborative workflows. Humans mostly cite to build new features, while agents cite to fix errors. Referenced pull requests also lived longer and took longer to review, suggesting heavier coordination effort.
arxiv-2604-04259: Wang and colleagues map tidal Love numbers onto Wilson coefficients in effective higher-curvature gravity theories. Love numbers describe how a black hole bulges under a companion's pull, while Wilson coefficients govern tidal marks in gravitational-wave signals. The team focuses on the static response of a non-spinning black hole, using control cases to pin down what a sound matching method needs. Those cases show where the standard general-relativity approach falls short, and a cubic-gravity computation closes a gap in the Love-to-Wilson link.
arxiv-2604-04759: Wang and thirteen colleagues run the first safety test of OpenClaw, an AI agent with full local access. They group an agent's lasting state into capability, identity, and knowledge, and test twelve attack scenes across four backbone models. Poisoning any one of those three parts lifts attack success from 24.6 percent to between 64 and 74 percent, with the toughest model more than tripling its risk. The best defence still fails 63.8 percent of the time under capability attacks, while file protection blocks 97 percent of injections but also stops updates.
arxiv-2604-05159: Amayuelas and seven colleagues present CovQValue, a quest-driven method for LLM test making. Greedy methods chase immediate gain, plateauing where deep branches need setup steps yielding zero new coverage. The method treats the program's branch structure as an environment and a map as a proxy guess. It feeds the map back to the model, generates test plans and picks the best by Q-values. It beats greedy picks on TestGenEval Lite, with 51 to 77 percent higher scores across three models.
arxiv-2604-05259: Chen and four colleagues study camera view selection for 3D reconstruction, building a rule for picking useful camera spots. Good views come from shrinking an estimate of Fisher Information Gain, favoring spots that show shape past cameras saw poorly. This gives COVER, a light coverage rule that skips costly transmittance estimates and stands up to noise and training shifts. In Nerfstudio, tried on real sets in fixed and embodied scenes, it beats active view choice methods on rebuild quality.
arxiv-2604-05359: Yi, Chen, Zhang, Shen, and Hu build a vision system that finds and describes distinctive image points, the anchors used to match views of the same scene. Instead of appearance alone, it combines meaning and shape clues for detection and description. One prediction head couples semantic labels with surface direction, while a second judges how stable each region's depth is. A fusion module then blends the cues into richer descriptors, and tests on four benchmarks back the design.
arxiv-2604-05459: Bremner, Elsholtz, and Ulas prove infinitely many three-dimensional Hilbert cubes hide entirely among the perfect squares. They count many reduced presentations with entries up to N and show the ratios of their entries fill the positive reals densely. The result turns a combinatorial curiosity about cubes of sums into a density theorem.
arxiv-2604-05559: Kostov proves new facts about the zeros of Ramanujan's partial theta function. For each q between 0 and 1, a vertical line with real part at most -5 separates real zeros on the left from complex zeros on the right. A similar split holds for negative q, with matching zero-free bands apart from one small exception.
arxiv-2604-05859: Berdica and five colleagues ask when language models are truly needed for contextual bandits mixing text and numbers. Their LLMP-UCB draws uncertainty from repeated language-model inference, yet light number bandits on text embeddings match or beat it at far lower cost. Embedding size tunes search versus payoff, and a shape-based diagnostic guides the choice between approaches.
arxiv-2604-06059: Tang and colleagues' 2026 paper spectroscopically confirms six new dual quasars and eleven offset quasars from the Subaru HSC-SSP program. Candidates came from SDSS quasar imaging, with companions within 0.6 to 4 arcseconds. Above redshift one and a half, dual black holes show high masses and luminosities with moderate Eddington ratios between one hundredth and four tenths. Dual fractions fall from one fifth to just over one percent below redshift four fifths. Between redshifts one and a half and three point three, they reach about six hundredths of a percent.
arxiv-2604-06159: Kaddour separates two questions that policy-gradient methods answer at once: which completions should gain probability, and how parameters should move to do it. His Target Policy Optimization builds a target from scored completions, weighting old probabilities by exponentiated scores, then fits the policy to that target with cross-entropy. Sampled-logit gradients equal the gap between policy and target, vanishing once they match. On tabular bandits, transformer tasks, and billion-parameter model training, it matches rivals on easy tasks and beats them clearly under sparse reward.
arxiv-2604-06259: Ahmed, Al-Badawi, and Sakallı study the optics of a Skyrmion black hole, focusing on the photon sphere, shadow, and trajectories. The Skyrme term and other spacetime geometry set the photon sphere location and shape its shadow. Parameter changes move results away from standard black hole geometries, hinting at nonlinear field effects. They also study Hawking radiation sparsity and energy emission spectra, and how both respond to Skyrme coupling and background parameters. The findings link nonlinear field contributions to black hole optics and modified gravity studies.
arxiv-2604-06559: Baiget and five colleagues build ExplainFuzz. Older fuzzers, chance grammars, and language models produce ill-formed inputs missing spreads and lacking clarity. From a context-free grammar, ExplainFuzz builds a grammar-aware circuit. Circuit control lets constraints such as GROUP BY shape sampling. Results show better sense and realism with perplexity drops. Native control enhances diversity under constraints. Against mutational fuzzing, bug rates rise 35 to 63 percent in SQL and 10 to 100 in XML. A learned distribution beats mutational fuzzing near seed inputs.
arxiv-2604-06759: Vekaria and three colleagues trace how lead marketing trades personal data and spawns spam. Instrumenting over 100 health lead-generation sites and watching 200 controlled phone numbers and email addresses, they follow data from web forms to consumer contact. Health details reach over 70 distinct third parties, and bought leads reveal sales to unvetted buyers, sometimes padded or invented with traits like health status and weight. The team fielded over 8,000 telemarketing calls, 600 texts, and 200 emails, often within seconds of submission, and found opt-outs weak, a picture 7,432 Better Business Bureau complaints confirm.
arxiv-2604-06859: Gerlach and four colleagues carve out a checkable corner of probabilistic hyperproperties, which compare chances across several runs of a random system. Full versions of these logics cannot be decided for Markov decision processes. The authors therefore focus on relations between event probabilities, covering reachability, safety, and repeated-visit goals that can also be combined. They give fast algorithms for some cases, hardness results for others, and a tool that beats general solvers by wide margins on shared benchmarks.
arxiv-2604-07159: Alouadi and four colleagues build SBBTS, a method for creating fake financial time series. It matches both the shape of returns and how they evolve over time, calibrating drift and volatility together. Older tools tend to fix volatility or ignore drift, so this joint approach fills a real gap. Tests on a standard volatility model and on S&P 500 data show better recovered parameters and stronger forecasts when fake data augments real training data.
arxiv-2604-07259: Girici, Hua, and Gündüz study how to split channel-training time across hops in a relay network that mimics a neural-network layer over the air. Accurate channel knowledge is essential, since a multi-hop amplify-and-forward network emulates a fully connected layer only when every link is well estimated. They test five heuristic schemes for allocating pilots across hops. Results show a clear trade-off between training overhead and classification accuracy, with balanced allocation and enough pilot power approaching the digital baseline.
arxiv-2604-07659: Li and three colleagues introduce Keys to Knowledge, a framework that replaces outside search in clinical models with key-based access. Large language models promise much in healthcare, yet hallucinations and thin detailed context undermine trust in urgent settings, while search needs costly searches over bases too slow for urgent care. Keys to Knowledge stores facts in the model's parameter space, enabling recall from key-value memory with no overhead. Activation-guided probe building and cross-attention reranking improve recall quality. Tests show top performance across four datasets.
arxiv-2604-07859: Li and five colleagues propose a communication framework that sends meaning instead of pixels. Traditional video coding serves human eyes and ships texture redundancy that wastes scarce bandwidth and delays machine decisions. Their Object-Attribute-Relation hierarchy fuses visual, textual, and audio streams into a graph built for choices, skipping pixel reconstruction entirely. A bandwidth-aware strategy rations bandwidth by priority as capacity shifts. Cross-modal priors from text and audio fill gaps, keeping machine choices reliable on dynamic channels.
arxiv-2604-08559: Ren and six colleagues survey how large language models reason about medicine, framing it as a cycle of abduction, deduction, and induction drawn from clinical thought. They sort methods into seven technical routes and test leading models under one shared setting, then introduce MR-Bench from real hospital data. The benchmark exposes a wide gap between exam style scores and accuracy on true clinical decisions.
arxiv-2604-08659: Khoury, Muntz, and Padilla propose a new route through the cosmological constant problem using a lapse function in a higher dimensional gravity theory. Inspired by Horava-Lifshitz gravity, they study a five dimensional spacetime where scaling differs along a compact extra dimension while keeping four dimensional Lorentz invariance. Varying the lapse in the deep infrared yields a global constraint akin to vacuum energy sequestering, cancelling radiative vacuum energy contributions at all orders.
arxiv-2604-08759: Huang, Tian, and Narayanan settle optimal multi bit watermarking of large language model output under worst case false alarm limits. Prior work set a lower bound on miss detection in the finite token regime and claimed a scheme reaching it, but the authors show that scheme is suboptimal. Two new encoding decoding constructions attain the bound, fully characterizing optimal performance. Framing watermark design as a linear program yields structural conditions for optimality, plus the failure mechanism of the old construction and tradeoffs between the two new schemes.
arxiv-2604-09859: Bhopi and six co-authors present PEACC, a digital calibrator for 21 cm telescopes needing precise wideband beam and gain calibration. PEACC sends Gaussian noise across a 1.2 GHz band, timed by a GPS clock, for aerial use. One unit flies on a drone; a reference unit feeds the data system directly, boosting weak-signal sensitivity and direct phase measurement. Chamber and drone-dish tests show the correlated channel beats auto-correlation throughout. The team claims three firsts: a clock-only free-space signal, a drone deployment, and beam measurements.
arxiv-2604-10059: Wiesheier, Moreno-Mateos, and Steinmann offer a new model for incompressible isotropic hyperelastic materials. Split formulas divide the energy into separate parts, which limits accuracy for hard cases. Their single two-variable B-spline surface spans the reachable invariant domain instead. Fitting uses uniform deformation modes and analytical stress relations, with no finite-element updating. Because spline coefficients enter linearly, fitting becomes a constrained linear least-squares task. The fit is fast, needs no start point, and beats split rivals.
arxiv-2604-10159: Wang and five colleagues define ODUTQA-MDC, a task for open-domain tabular question answering where questions are underspecified or uncertain. Their benchmark is the first for this setting. It holds 209 tables with 25,105 question-answer pairs, a fine-grained labeling scheme, and a dynamic clarification interface that mimics user feedback. Their MAIC-TQA framework uses several agents to spot ambiguities, clarify them through dialogue, and refine answers. Tests validate both benchmark and framework as a key resource for conversational tabular question answering.
arxiv-2604-10559: Jonsson derives Kepler style period laws for many body systems by dimension counting. His broadened dimensional analysis first recovers the two body law up to a constant. The same tool then stretches that law to n-body systems of both classical and quantum kinds. Results match Sun's classical guess and the Semay and Sun quantum guess. The work thus finds periods without ever solving the motion equations.
arxiv-2604-10859: Ziashahabi, He, and Avestimehr test message-passing backends for cross-silo federated learning, where strong servers team up over varied links and big models strain the net. Their tests cover MPI, gRPC, and PyTorch RPC for single-link and end-to-end speed across model sizes under lifelike net conditions. They also add gRPC+S3, a hybrid backend fixing current limits for big-model transfer across far-flung sites, up to 3.8 times faster end to end than gRPC. The results guide backend choice and setup for given tasks and nets.
arxiv-2604-10959: Zheng and fourteen colleagues build Ozone, a shared platform for transportation research organized in hardware, data, model, and evaluation layers, plus a prototype layer for deployed applications. Its data layer joins vehicle paths, traffic conflicts, rebuilt crashes, and twin maps under one path schema, covering nineteen datasets at fifty-nine sites in eight countries. Shared converters align coordinates, object classes, bounding boxes, and motion fields, and a study reports setup time falling by eighty-five percent. Case studies cover human factors and automated-driving safety testing.
arxiv-2604-11259: Lin and seven colleagues personalize mobile GUI agents for privacy with TIPO, trajectory-induced preference optimization. Privacy-first users favor protective steps such as refusing permissions and logging out, so their action paths differ structurally from utility-first users, which destabilizes standard preference training. TIPO weights key privacy steps by preference intensity and gates padding noise, improving persona alignment and distinction while keeping task success strong, at 65.60 percent success on their privacy dataset.
arxiv-2604-11459: Lerman argues that troubling outcomes of feed algorithms stem from goal mismatch. Systems tuned for clicks, views, and engagement capture attention well, yet their goals diverge from the human goals predictions should serve. She traces the gap to three mechanisms: fast reactions win over careful judgment, feedback loops couple user behavior with machine learning, and crowd dynamics amplify effects at scale. Accurate individual predictions can thus yield bad social outcomes, and she outlines research to study and fix the mismatch.
arxiv-2604-11859: Ferreira and Ganapathisubramani apply generalised least squares (GLS) to the log-law velocity profile of turbulent boundary layers, setting a standard way to gauge its parameters. Unlike plain or weighted least squares, the method carries a full covariance matrix of residuals, worked out from primitive-variable errors. Test data mimicking hot-wire readings on a moving rig flag the biggest error sources and fixes in advance. The study also offers a fitting routine needing no preset log-region spot or size, with open-source Python code to download.
arxiv-2604-12059: Schwartz sorts solutions to the four-color problem for sphere triangulations with degree sequence of sixes followed by fours into combinatorial types. Each generic type is parametrised by integer lattice points inside a rational polyhedral convex cone of dimension at least four. An integral quadratic form on the cone has a diagonal part equal, on a lattice point, to three times the triangle count of the corresponding triangulation. He relates this structure to the octahedral stratum of Thurston's moduli space of flat cone structures on the sphere.
arxiv-2604-12559: Peng Wang and four colleagues edit language models with fine-grained facts, not whole texts. Existing editing often memorizes text wholesale without reliable fact access. FABLE splits fact injection from text generation in two stages. Discrete facts anchor in shallow layers first. Minimal updates to deeper layers then yield coherent text. The split matches the one-way flow of Transformer generation. A new UnFine benchmark tests fact-level editing systematically. Tests show stronger fine-grained answering with top holistic editing kept.
arxiv-2604-12659: Kaiqi Hu and four colleagues benchmark vision-language models on candlestick charts. Prior tests fail to isolate whether visual understanding truly aids price forecasts. Most setups use single-period or tabular inputs. Analysts read multi-scale charts for trend and turning points. The team builds a multi-scale dataset with a standard evaluation framework. Scoring mixes confusion matrices with information coefficient series. Most models shine only in persistent uptrends or downtrends. They show weak prediction in common scenarios, with bias and poor horizon sensitivity.
arxiv-2604-12959: Anzhelika V. Buskina and Vladimir A. Zyuzin model a heavy fermion d-f hybrid. Two fermion species carry very different masses. Mixing at the crossing point leaves no true insulating gap, keeping a heavy hybrid at the Fermi level. The model explains SmB6 low-temperature behavior: linear specific heat, saturating resistance, and frequency-dependent optical conductivity. Conductivity peaks broadly at twice the mixing value with a low-frequency tail.
arxiv-2604-13659: Ciacchi and four colleagues explain a puzzle in salt water: water moves faster in cesium iodide solutions yet slower in table-salt solutions. Using molecular dynamics with a machine-learned many-body force field trained in the MACE framework, they reproduce both anomalies. The gain over the earlier DeePMD approach is largest for table salt. Strong sodium-water binding in the first hydration shell slows water there, while a loose iodide shell lets water exchange fast in cesium iodide.
arxiv-2604-13859: Zlatanov and three colleagues decouple STIRAP from microwave dressing in trapped Rydberg ion gates. Dipole-dipole interaction promises sub-microsecond gates, such as a two-qubit gate in strontium ions via joint STIRAP and microwave interaction. That protocol distorts the dark state and risks intermediate-state decay. Instead, STIRAP and microwave dressing run in separate stages, preventing interference. The scheme reaches 99.93 percent fidelity, beating prior gates, with a speedup to 400 nanoseconds via shaped pulses. The phase is then set by interaction strength, via nonresonant chirping.
arxiv-2604-13959: Choi, Park, and Kim propose Artificial Tripartite Intelligence, a sensor-first design for physical AI that splits work across three layers. A Brainstem layer guards reflexive safety and signal integrity, a Cerebellum layer calibrates sensors continuously, and a cerebral layer handles skills, coordination, and deep reasoning. On a mobile camera test, adaptive sensing lifts accuracy from 53.8 percent to 88 percent while cutting remote inference calls.
arxiv-2604-14359: The LDMX Collaboration sizes up a second hunt for the Light Dark Matter eXperiment, an electron-beam fixed-target search for sub-GeV dark matter. Beyond its flagship missing-momentum hunt for invisible particles, the team simulates visibly decaying, long-lived dark photons and axion-like particles that couple to electrons. With realistic detector response and backgrounds modeled in Geant4, the search reaches sensitivity rivaling running experiments. Covering both invisible and visible signatures widens the experiment's sweep of the light dark sector.
arxiv-2604-14459: Desai and Nair ask whether language models trained on child-sized data build one shared representation for filler-gap dependencies across constructions. Using distributed alignment search, they probe models trained on varying BabyLM data amounts for transfer between wh-questions and topicalization, which differ greatly in input frequency. Shared yet item-sensitive mechanisms seem to develop with limited data. Still, models need far more data than children to reach similar generalizations, suggesting language-specific biases belong in models of language learning.
arxiv-2604-14559: Ugur and Webb use computer simulations to probe how water first stiffens chitosan, then softens it, as water content rises. Elastic moduli show a contest between weakening polymer-polymer bonds and strengthening polymer-water bonds, with their balance setting properties. They offer a simple model in which open free-volume regions drive polymer mobility, covering both stiffening and softening of elastic properties. Free-volume access, they show, depends on links among additive-accessible volume regions, a finding that may guide design of chitosan and other wet biopolymers.
arxiv-2604-14659: Yogesh, Bhat, Gangopadhyay, and Sami revisit quintessential inflation under Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity, where a scalar field coupled to Gauss-Bonnet shifts inflation. Atacama Cosmology Telescope results put the scalar spectral index at 0.9743, plus or minus three-thousandths, pushing that inflation near or past the two-sigma edge. Exponential and sech couplings shift values into ACT's one-sigma region, while tanh coupling stays out. Viable reheat paths emerge without a potential minimum, at levels matching Big Bang nucleosynthesis bounds.
arxiv-2604-14859: Krsnik, Novko, Kugler, Barišić, and Held study plasmon modes in Sr2RuO4, where strong electron correlations rewrite the weak picture. Their ab initio approach joins density functional and dynamical mean-field theory and settles conflicting energy-loss spectroscopy results. Correlations reproduce the plasmon dispersion while giving a large width below the electron-hole continuum. An extra high-energy peak from transitions between incoherent features and a sharp rise in spread, akin to photoemission falls, both emerge as genuine correlation effects.
arxiv-2604-14959: Suzuki and 15 others show 1-terahertz all-optical quantum teleportation, skipping electrical feed-forward near 100 MHz. Sending Bell outcomes by light, they sent vacuum states across the THz band and random coherent wavepackets 42 ps wide. Fidelities reached 0.784 for broadband vacuum states and 0.770 for dynamic coherent wavepackets, both above the classical limit of 0.5. Optical speeds now hinge only on the nonlinear medium's 1-ps response, not wire links. The method anchors THz-clock quantum computers and a telecom-ready quantum internet.
arxiv-2604-15059: Bakhale and Sao build a scanner-proof checker for motion flaws in brain MRI scans. Their hybrid net pairs a layered image encoder with attention that weighs broad patterns, so it can spot ringing and blur while ignoring site-specific brightness quirks. Trained on 200 subjects, it scored near-perfect marks on familiar sites and about 76 percent on 17 unseen sites with no retraining. The team reads this as proof that attention can learn flaw signatures that travel across machines.
arxiv-2604-15259: Labovich studies looped transformers, networks that repeat one layer to spend extra compute on harder problems, and asks which design choices let them generalize instead of memorizing training tricks. His fixed-point framework tracks reachability, input sensitivity, and geometry, showing that memory plus outer normalization yields stable, reachable fixed points. Tests on chess, sudoku, and prefix sums match the theory, and a new internal memory placement beats standard placement on sudoku.
arxiv-2604-15359: Nadimi and Zheng present AutoFlows++, a two-stage framework for mining message flows from system-on-chip communication traces. Local mining pulls simple patterns from single interfaces, then global mining composes them into higher-level flows spanning components. Tests on synthetic traces and GEM5 SoC models show clearly better flow-extraction accuracy than prior methods, aiding verification, performance analysis, and post-silicon debugging.
arxiv-2604-15559: Dang, Xie, and Younis show for the first time that harmful agent habits can pass from teacher to student through distillation, even when training runs are scrubbed of explicit danger words. A teacher with a deletion bias distills into students that delete at a 100 percent rate versus a 5 percent baseline on safe tasks. A Bash teacher's chmod-first preference transfers at 30 to 55 percent versus 0 to 10 percent. Keyword sanitation alone cannot block the transfer.
arxiv-2604-15859: Qin and Andriushchenko present QuantSightBench, a benchmark that grades language models on quantitative forecasting through prediction intervals rather than single-point guesses or simple choices. They force a sense of scale, fit across confidence levels, and tuning across a full range of results. Testing 11 frontier and open-weight models, they find none reaches 90 percent coverage. The best, Gemini 3.1 Pro at 79.1 percent, still falls over 10 points short, with models too sure of themselves at extreme sizes.
arxiv-2604-15959: Yang, Katt, and Kaski propose STAGE-BO, a multi-objective Bayesian optimization method for several costly goals at once. Existing methods struggle with coverage, scale, constraints, and preferences. By finding the Pareto point with the largest uncovered gap, the method sets adaptive limits that turn the problem into a sequence of smaller limited problems, solved by constrained expected improvement. It gives uniform Pareto spread without hypervolume math, and handles constraints and user wishes. Tests on synthetic and real-world benchmarks show better coverage and competitive hypervolume results.
arxiv-2604-16059: Amini and eight colleagues present terahertz electron bunches for injection into laser-plasma wake accelerators. Such machines offer huge gradients in setups, but nonlinear effects hurt beam quality. Bunches from radio-frequency sources suffer compression and mismatch, causing energy jitter and beam growth. This control locks timing to the laser and squeezes beams to under 10 femtoseconds before entry. Models show GeV-scale boost with quality, energy jitter and spread at 0.2 percent. The concept aids multi-stage laser machines and lasers.
arxiv-2604-16159: Nair studies halfspace separation in geodesic convexity on graphs. A set is convex if it holds every shortest path between its members. A halfspace is a convex set whose complement is also convex. The question is whether two given sets can be split by complementary halfspaces. Known to be hard in general graphs, the problem turns out to be solvable in polynomial time for matroid basis graphs, weakly bridged graphs, and pseudo-modular graphs.
arxiv-2604-16259: Mittal, Gagnon, and Lajoie ask whether task-reward reinforcement learning truly teaches frontier models new skills, or merely sharpens skills they already hold. They compare distribution sharpening with task-reward learning head to head, using reinforcement learning to run both. From first principles, they show sharpening has unfavourable optima and is fundamentally unstable. Tests on three small instruct models and math datasets confirm sharpening gains little, while task rewards help robust performance greatly.
arxiv-2604-16359: Ma, Yang and Chen survey how large language models are being used to read and interpret software logs. Their review covers 145 papers across seven tasks, from writing and tidying log statements to spotting anomalies, forecasting failures, tracing root causes and summarizing events. They sort the field by task and design pattern, then weigh evidence on evaluation, data, reproducibility and deployment risks such as hallucinations and privacy. The result is a map of what works, what remains fragile under changing logs, and where reliable adoption still needs proof.
arxiv-2604-16459: Sha and colleagues address fault intensity diagnosis in smart manufacturing, where ignoring links between fault classes hurts practical use. Their deep hierarchical knowledge loss framework maps classes of the same attribute through a hierarchical tree loss with tree-based positive and negative constraints. A focal variant extends the idea, adaptive weights use tree height, and a group tree triplet loss with a dynamic margin models boundary structure across classes. The joint losses sharpened recognition of subtle faults, beating recent leading methods on four real industrial datasets, including three cavitation sets.
arxiv-2604-16559: Srivastava and colleagues study polynomial multiproofs for availability in blockchain light clients. Light clients verify availability without blocks, fetching cells from a peer network and checking commitments. Giving each cell its own KZG proof creates bandwidth and verification overhead. Their design verifies cell values with one proof over a micro-domain. It adjusts generation, dissemination, retrieval and verification in the stack. Evaluated in Avail, it cut proof size, verifier CPU and memory use. Costs fell by up to 45 percent against a baseline, while grouped-retrieval trade-offs became clear.
arxiv-2604-16659: Roh and colleagues study how fine-tuning breaks alignment in audio language models. Audio samples can sit near harmful content in words or sound. They evaluate models with a framework splitting distance into semantic, acoustic and mixed axes. The axis depends on architecture, set by each encoder and projector. Benign tuning lifts jailbreak success from single digits to 87 percent. Tuning silences circuits while frozen encoders keep signals, so models spot harm but stop refusing. Filtering away from harmful embeddings and a text prompt cut jailbreak success to near zero.
arxiv-2604-16759: Liang and Li give a weak solution of Inverse Treblecross, the avoidance version of Treblecross. This version bans completing a line of three X's. An empty board of n cells counts as a P-position when n leaves remainder 0, 2, 3, 6 or 9 on division by 10. It has value 1 when n leaves remainder 1, 4, 5, 7 or 8, so the empty-board sequence is purely periodic with period 10. The proof introduces characteristic functions and regular positions, showing a reduction move splits a position into a sum with preserved or inverted sign product.
arxiv-2604-17259: Goel and four colleagues present HORIZON, a benchmark that reformulates user modeling along dataset, task, and evaluation axes, built from Amazon Reviews covering 54M users and 35M items. Unlike prior benchmarks focused on short sessions, HORIZON challenges models to generalize across domains, users, and time, with tasks on temporal generalization and unseen users. Benchmarking sequential recommendation architectures alongside LLM baselines using long histories, the authors show a gap between current methods and real demands. HORIZON thus stands as a foundation for robust cross-domain user models.
arxiv-2604-17359: Keough audits language models asked to play psychiatric patients, comparing 28,800 simulated cases against survey-weighted clinical anchors. Case by case the output looks sound, with over 97 percent of elevated cases satisfying the DSM-5 gateway rule. As populations, though, every group comes back inflated, and about 18 percent screen at the treatment threshold against under 8 percent of real adults. Real racial disparities vanish or flip, symptom patterns reorganize by cohort, and repeat draws shift a third of patients between severity bands, so plausible cases compose impossible populations.
arxiv-2604-17959: Yuxiang Zhao and four colleagues present CoEvoer, a one-stage transformer framework for upper-body expressive pose and shape estimation in augmented and virtual reality. Current methods struggle with face and hand parameters and generalize poorly to unconstrained images. CoEvoer lets body parts interact at the feature level. Large regions like the torso then supply global context and position cues for the face and hands, while fine local details refine nearby parts. The framework leads upper-body benchmarks and generalizes well to unseen wild images.
arxiv-2604-18259: Gal questions a recent MAMI measurement that assigns a sharp pion-momentum line to hypertriton weak decay. That assignment yields an exceptionally large hypertriton binding energy. Gal instead reads the line as decay of the ground state of helium-7 with a lambda particle into lithium-7, and traces what that reading implies for the helium-7 binding energy. The note offers an alternative interpretation rather than a new measurement.
arxiv-2604-18559: Lee and five colleagues investigate how to perturb AF3 latent representations to capture alternate protein states. AlphaFold models predict one main shape for most well-ordered proteins but struggle with others. Past efforts used ad hoc tweaks, still wasteful, failing to recover major modes every time. ConforNets are channel-wise affine transforms of pre-Pairformer latents, tuning AF3 states for reuse. They lead all multi-state benchmarks on unsupervised generation of other states, and in transfer tasks, training on one source protein induces a shared family change.
arxiv-2604-18959: Majhi, Agnihotri, and Mondal compare physical and augmented reality card games for refresher training of ASHA workers in India. Conventional training has proved weak at building capacity for child immunization work, while health workers increasingly carry smartphones. Two tools teach the child immunization schedule through play, one physical and one AR based. Tests before and after play show the AR version wins on learning, knowledge retention, and engagement, thanks to its interactive and intuitive play.
arxiv-2604-19459: Kim, Poiroux, and Bosselut test whether frontier language models game formalization in Lean 4 proofs of plain-language logical reasoning. Formal verification guarantees proof validity but not formalization faithfulness, and the gap is acute when models build axiom systems from scratch with no libraries. Testing GPT-5 and DeepSeek-R1 on 303 first-order logic problems, they compare unified generation with a two-stage pipeline splitting formalization and proving. Despite compilation rates of 87 to 99 percent, they find no systematic gaming in unified generation, as models prefer reporting failure over forcing proofs.
arxiv-2604-19659: Burini and Knopoff extend the Kinetic Theory of Active Particles into a multiscale version, MS-KTAP, that adds a sub-microscopic layer of interacting entities to the picture of collective behavior. In their view, the activity variable emerges from lower-scale control processes. It is also shaped by interactions across higher scales, rather than being fixed at one level. The paper argues that living systems need this richer frame because single-scale models, even refined ones, miss features like varied behavior, adaptive choices, and nonlinear effects.
arxiv-2604-19959: Aitken, Reimitz, and Ritz probe boosted sub-GeV dark matter, light dark particles kicked to high speed by cosmic ray collisions in the atmosphere. They extend past sensitivity estimates to higher masses by modeling proton bremsstrahlung, radiation emitted when protons scatter. For vector-mediated models, production peaks when mediator masses sit near the rho and omega resonances. They compare reach across direct detectors LZ and PandaX-4T and neutrino detectors Borexino and Super-K.
arxiv-2604-20059: Xu, Gruber, and van der Laan study TMLE targeting and truncation for average treatment effects under practical positivity violations. Loss-weighted targeting can bias results a lot versus clever-covariate targeting, while too little truncation inflates spread for the latter approach. Fixed truncation rules with constants 5 or 6 prove robust defaults, though the best choice varies with sample size and setting. A Lepski-type adaptive rule with a brake improves stability, and targeted bootstrap estimation stays stable across truncation levels.
arxiv-2604-20559: The ATLAS Collaboration studies photonuclear jet production in ultra-peripheral lead-lead collisions at 5.02 TeV. The study asks how jet output depends on forward neutron emission from either nucleus. At lower photon fractions, where the non-diffractive leads, the nuclear parton distribution can be probed in collisions leaving the nucleus intact. The cross-section shape in collisions differs from that in collisions with forward neutron emission, at six sigma significance. At large fractions, large-impact-parameter collisions show no changes to parton distributions, unlike smaller-impact-parameter collisions.
arxiv-2604-21159: Jesse Zymet and four colleagues automate red-teaming by composing attacker instructions adaptively instead of at random or by trial and error alone. Their reinforcement-learning bandit balances trying new combinations against exploiting winners, steering attacks toward each target's weak spots while keeping them diverse. The method beats random composition and recent adaptive rivals on Harmbench, and its edge survives transfer to new models.
arxiv-2604-21359: Song Gao and three colleagues model ride-hailing traffic balance with vehicles, empty or hired, making step-by-step order and link choices to maximize total future return. The model builds in rivalry among empty vehicles for passengers and congestion from road use at the link level. Balance becomes a fixed-point system whose existence they prove, with relaxed fixed-point iteration methods and convergence results for special networks. Ignoring congestion or drivers' forward-looking behavior, ablation studies show, can bias policy evaluation a lot.
arxiv-2604-21659: Kilian Unterguggenberger and colleagues demonstrate an all-optical trick for taming spectral diffusion in single-photon emitters, a wobble in emission color caused by noisy surroundings. Driving a two-level solid-state emitter with a periodic train of optical pi-pulses during its excited lifetime shifts the emission peak to a chosen laser frequency. It also narrows the broadened line close to its lifetime limit. About half the absorption can be steered to a freely selected target frequency, opening the method to many emitter types.
arxiv-2604-21759: Zhu and Zhang model multi-band light curves of 80 broad-lined Type Ic supernovae, including 11 linked to long gamma-ray bursts, with a magnetar engine plus nickel-56 decay. All data fit a magnetar central engine well. Median nickel mass, spin period, polar field, and ejecta mass are 0.18 solar masses, about 2 milliseconds, about 4 times 10 to the 15 gauss, and about 2 solar masses. A universal ejecta-mass versus spin correlation supports a unified magnetar-powered stripped-envelope picture.
arxiv-2604-21859: Kumar and five colleagues cut errors in gravitational-wave parameter estimation for binary black hole mergers from LIGO-Virgo's first three observing runs. They reanalyse events flagged as potentially affected, using models that build uncertainty in waveform phase and amplitude into broad priors. The method cuts errors even from glitches near a signal and from deglitching. Results become consistent across waveform models and across raw and deglitched data, including for GW191109 and GW200129.
arxiv-2604-22359: Huang and three colleagues test whether K-star and Sigma-star can bind into molecular states. In a one-boson-exchange model, they build rho, omega and pi exchanges and solve the Schrödinger equation by Gaussian expansion. Binding energies are computed across angular momentum and isospin channels. Mixed S-D states with spin-parity one-half minus form only in the three-halves channel. States with spin-parity three-halves minus and five-halves minus also bind. The analysis backs reading N(2250) and Delta(2200) as molecular candidates.
arxiv-2604-22459: Kozhemiachenko and Sedlár build a fuzzy modal logic for reasoning about chance, action, and knowledge together. It can state claims such as how an action raises or lowers the chance that someone knows a fact. Meaning is given on Kripke frames, networks of possible worlds, fitted with probability measures. The authors then map how hard it is to decide whether formulas can be true, across the full language and varied fragments. For several fragments they pin down polynomial-time decidability, marking where the logic stays tractable.
arxiv-2604-22559: Husain, Andika, and Arifyanto study a quasar-companion pair near redshift 6, a window on how nucleus activity shapes its surroundings during reionization. ALMA data on ionized carbon emission and far-infrared continuum trace cold gas and dust-reprocessed radiation from star formation and nucleus heat. The team compares the quasar host with its companion galaxy. Both galaxies show typical carbon-line to far-infrared brightness ratios for star-forming galaxies, with no carbon-line deficit, showing stellar heating dominates their gas energetics. No active-nucleus outflow is found.
arxiv-2604-22759: Ao, Zou, Wei, Wang, and Guo improve related-question search on community sites like Stack Overflow by treating search as a chat, not a single static match. Their TeCQR model builds dialogues from tag-enhanced clarifying questions and adds a noise-tolerant stage that weighs question-tag likeness, filtering shaky feedback. Two-stage offline training then exploits links among queries, questions, and tags.
arxiv-2604-22859: Staufenbiel presents Adjacency Sampling, a faster but partial method for finding Bell inequalities. Such inequalities certify quantum correlations and underpin device-independent key distribution. Enumerating every inequality means solving a hard facet problem on the Bell polytope, so the new method trades completeness for speed. Even so, it reproduces all known classes on previously solved polytopes. Where no complete enumeration exists it vastly expands known lists, including more than 25 times the earlier count in one scenario and nearly triple in another.
arxiv-2604-23059: Karacan and four co-authors analyze implicit framing in obstetric counseling notes for patients cleared for both vaginal birth after cesarean and repeat cesarean. A cohort of 2,024 history and physical notes is built from tabular clinical data plus a language-model mining pipeline tied to grounded, verbatim evidence. A zero-shot framework then sorts advice segments into framing groups for how birth options are put. Risk-focused language takes a much larger share in repeat cesarean notes than in vaginal birth notes, with differences backed by statistical testing.
arxiv-2604-23159: Li studies the 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes equations with a Fourier spectral method and a fourth-order Runge-Kutta time scheme. The analysis sets spectral accuracy, resolution rules, and an energy-based regularity frame. From these, Li proves exponential and algebraic convergence plus a test tying numerical blowup to loss of regularity. The work yields diagnostics for spotting possible finite-time singular events.
arxiv-2604-23359: Gissler and Breuer show with a flapping robot in a wind tunnel that faster flapping amplifies longitudinal static stability, even stabilising an unstable flier. Stability depends not only on static margin but also on Strouhal number. Measurements across frequencies and wind speeds match a quasi-steady blade-element model and its low-order approximation. Higher pitch stiffness at higher Strouhal numbers comes from higher mean effective wind speed, with amplitude effects flipping sign between high and low Strouhal numbers.
arxiv-2604-23459: Hagag and colleagues study how the architecture of multi-agent AI systems, rather than any single agent, shapes security. Across three settings and thirteen designs, they vary agent roles, communication patterns, and memory access, tracking where attacks are refused, intercepted, or completed. Multi-agent setups prove more vulnerable than standalone agents in most configurations, with attack success shifting nearly fourfold, and no single design emerges as universally safest.
arxiv-2604-23659: Fu and Po introduce a peak-valley mechanism for strong Hilbert space fragmentation in one-dimensional integer spin chains, a form of ergodicity breaking without disorder. A simple local rule labels computational-basis states by emergent quantum numbers that follow alternating peaks and valleys in a geometric picture. Known fragmented models and their fragmentation-breaking variants both fit the framework, which also constructs new fragmented models.
arxiv-2604-24259: Basa and colleagues present COLIBRI, the French-Mexican Ground Follow-up Telescope for SVOM, a 1.3 meter rapid optical scope. Built for prompt multi-band burst views, it gives subarcsecond counterpart spots for follow-up studies. A fully self-running system manages the workflow, from alert receipt to target identification. Testing confirms it meets design specs, and the paper rates its results on SVOM alerts.
arxiv-2604-24759: Bazzi and colleagues measure the formation and lifetime of giant molecular clouds using a catalog of 108,466 clouds identified in JWST imaging across 66 galaxies at 30 parsec resolution. Clouds up to 100,000 solar masses form on average in 20 million years, while more massive clouds take up to 100 million years. Formation runs fastest in galaxy centers, typically 5 to 10 million years shorter than in disks, driven by intense star formation, dense gas and strong supersonic compressions. Star formation stays inefficient, since cloud lifetime is only about 1 percent of the molecular depletion time.
arxiv-2604-24859: Iyer and four colleagues build single-anyon Bloch states in an ideal band from Laughlin wavefunctions. The states give a basis to compute anyon dispersion efficiently. Fractional Chern insulators are zero-field analogs of quantum Hall states. Their anyons feel a finite-flux field from a Berry phase. The spectrum shows an m-fold degeneracy in the reduced zone. Bandwidth is controlled by uneven quantum geometry. It grows linearly at weak modulation and saturates at strong modulation.
arxiv-2604-25259: Yu introduces DGLight, a critic-guided framework adapting a pretrained language model to traffic signal control. DGLight first trains a CoLight-based Deep Q-Network critic to estimate action values at crossings. The frozen critic scores actions and tunes the policy with Group Relative Policy Optimization. The controller maps traffic states to reasoning traces and signal decisions from dense per-state supervision. On Jinan and Hangzhou benchmarks, DGLight beats compared LLM controllers, matches strong reinforcement-learning baselines and transfers well to unseen city data sets.
arxiv-2604-25459: Jia and 41 colleagues put forth GS-Playground, a high-throughput photorealistic sim for vision-led robot learning. Huge systems boosted body-sense movement, but stay untapped for vision tasks, since rendering costs too much. GS-Playground joins a novel physics engine to a batch 3D Gaussian Splatting pipeline for high-fidelity sync. It reaches 10,000 frames per second at 640 by 480, easing visual learning. An automated Real2Sim workflow rebuilds lifelike, physics-true scenes. Tests on movement, navigation, and manipulation show it bridges perceptual and physical gaps across varied tasks.
arxiv-2604-25559: Hahner and 24 colleagues extend the ECMWF data-driven system AIFS to model the atmosphere and surface ocean jointly, with waves and sea ice included. Past models kept the two parts apart, but the joint model learns links across the whole air-sea interface straight from data. The team handles missing values over land and multi-scale time dynamics. For nearly all tested marine variables, skill at medium-range lead times gains about a day over physics-based models. The model also predicts wave swell and tropical-cyclone cold wakes.
arxiv-2604-25859: Fang, Chen, and Cai argue that future prediction in world action models is a compressible correction to action denoising. The authors define privileged foresight as the true-future minus current-frame prediction gap. Their distillation moves that residual from a teacher into a small add-on module for a current-only student. LIBERO and RoboTwin tests show gains at negligible latency.
arxiv-2604-26059: Di Guardia, Ehrhard, and Faggian bring compositional principles and a typing discipline to quantum Bayesian networks. These networks are graphical models for causal relations and measurement probabilities across classical and quantum data. Their compositional semantics matches the standard factor-based reading when all causes are classical. In the purely quantum case it reduces to tensor networks. A typed formalism built on linear logic proof-nets then guarantees well-behaved composition of systems, proved sound and complete with respect to quantum Bayesian networks.
arxiv-2604-26259: Bridges asked about linear maps between Banach spaces: if an input is small in norm, must it sit near the kernel? The kernel is the set of inputs the map sends to zero. Drawing on Z-stability, he gave a constructive yes for maps that cover the target space. The maps must also vary continuously in sequence and have a located kernel. The note settles when closeness to the kernel is guaranteed.
arxiv-2604-26359: Gasser, Segers, and Ragone built a unified stats framework for pinning heatwaves, as space-time events, on climate change. Their generative model for daily temperature fields splits edge behavior from space-time dependence, joining Bayesian spatial quantile regression, a shifting extreme-value model for tails, and a copula model for dependence in extremes. Run on a CMIP6 climate model, it set factual scenes against counterfactual ones for event-level attribution. The approach catches heatwave traits that standard edge-only methods miss.
arxiv-2604-26659: Proskurnin improves the best known upper bound for coranks of equivariantly stable singularities for groups of prime order. He proves that the maximal corank of a simple Zp-invariant germ grows without bound as p increases. It behaves asymptotically like a logarithm, so the earlier bound holds up to order of magnitude. The result sharpens what is known about how complex such symmetric singularities can become as the prime grows.
arxiv-2604-27259: Venkatesan, Chen, and Liu introduce VTBench, a multi-mode framework for time-series sorting using chart-based representations alongside raw sequences. Most deep models use raw numbers alone, overlooking alternative encodings. Texture encodings such as Gramian Angular Fields and Recurrence Plots turn series into images but need heavy prep work and read less clearly. Chart visualizations read more naturally and show promise in specific domains, yet lacked thorough evaluation across chart types, encodings, and datasets, which VTBench supplies.
arxiv-2604-27459: Calderón and three others show that tracing out a Galilean-invariant bath breaks boost covariance of the motion, while shifts and turns survive. Analysis of the Hu-Paz-Zhang master equation locates the break in the dissipative anticommutator term. The damping coefficient, by the fluctuation-dissipation theorem, links to bath-driven momentum diffusion, so Galilean invariance, that theorem, and boost symmetry cannot all hold for a bath. A ratio marks the crossing, with cold atoms and chilled molecules at its edge, and parametric driving cuts breaking over a cycle.
arxiv-2604-27659: Huang and seven colleagues bring flexible endorsement to order-execute blockchains with FlexTender, built on Tendermint. Modern private blockchains need endorsement rules defined per contract or state object, which Fabric handles with execute-order-validate, while most systems, including ChainMaker, use order-execute. It embeds them into consensus, removing problem transactions from an ordered list deterministically, keeping censorship resistance and decentralization intact. On an Ethereum USDT workload, it reaches up to 10.6 times the throughput of an execute-order-validate test on the same platform.
arxiv-2604-28059: Al Hafiz and Podobas present NeuroRing, a spiking neural network accelerator built as a two-way ring across one or more FPGAs. It plugs into current workflows through the NEST simulator and keeps the reference model's activity stats on a cortical microcircuit test. It also runs that full-scale circuit faster than real time with strong energy efficiency, suiting brain simulation and event-driven computing.
arxiv-2605-00459:
Maksym Nechepurenko stress-tests his own framework for detecting information leakage, possible insider trading, on the prediction market Polymarket. His deadline-resolved leakage score had worked as a single-case proof of concept.
